ai-&-i-by-every.bio: Podcast: How Stripe Is Building for an Agent-native World

html_en:
From new fraud vectors targeting AI compute credits to the emergence of "agent HR" roles, Silicon Valley is grappling with the practical realities of an increasingly autonomous internet economy.

The Agent Economy's Growing Pains

The internet is no longer just humans clicking through websites. As Emily Glassberg Sands from Stripe explained on Dan Shipper's AI & I podcast, we're witnessing a fundamental shift:
"The Internet has this new kind of actor on it. Over time, this actor, these agents will become the predominant actors on the Internet... basically every layer of the stack starts to need an evolution."
This evolution is creating entirely new categories of problems and opportunities. Zara Zhang captured the organizational implications perfectly: "We should start thinking about the IT/internal tools team as more like 'HR for agents'" The shift is already prompting companies to create new roles. Aaron Levie from Box shared his company's plans to hire "agent engineering roles for *internal* functions" — technical positions that will wire up business systems and build secure, governed agents for internal workflows. As Levie noted, these roles span multiple teams and require both technical expertise and process understanding.

Fraud Moves Up the Stack

The agent economy has fundamentally changed what fraud looks like. Where payment fraud once meant stolen credit cards, today's fraudsters are after something more valuable: compute credits.
"Increasingly, actually, and I was in a meeting with one of our very large AI users today, fraudsters are stealing compute, and that's a very different type of problem," Sands explained. "In AI, every prompt, every image that gets generated, every API request has a very real cost attached to it."
The numbers are staggering. Sands revealed that about 7% of AI company sign-ups are multi-account abusers claiming new user credits repeatedly. One large AI company was seeing only 4% of free trials convert to paid customers, with each trial costing $25 in LLM spend — meaning $625 in costs per actual paying customer.
"Free trial abuse has 4x-ed in the last six months," Sands noted, with Stripe now blocking 250,000 fraudulent free trials weekly for one major customer.

The Reality Check on Agent Usability

While the hype around AI agents continues, those actually building with them are finding the experience more challenging than advertised. Aditya Agarwal shared some brutally honest observations after extensive work with OpenClaw and Hermes:
"Most people who rave about OpenClaw, HermesAgent etc. have not actually used it. Facts... Agents are developer products today. They are so so so far from being consumer grade in terms of delight, simplicity, reliability etc."
Agarwal compared the current state to "running Linux in the early 2000s" — requiring extensive configuration and setup before reaching basic utility. This sentiment was echoed by Peter Yang, who noted performance issues even with basic Claude web UI usage: "I often now have to wait 3-5 seconds randomly for it to respond."

Building Better Agent Experiences

Despite the challenges, developers are pushing forward. Peter Steinberger demonstrated practical progress by integrating automated code review into ClawSweeper, creating a system that "loops until it stops finding new issues." Meanwhile, Ryo Lu announced that users can now "build your own agent systems with Cursor – the same multi-model harness, on local and cloud."

Enterprise AI Acceleration

While agent UX remains rough around the edges, enterprise adoption is accelerating at unprecedented rates. Sands revealed that AI companies are hitting $30M ARR in just 18 months — three times faster than the 2018 SaaS cohort. This growth is coming from net new spending rather than cannibalized software budgets, suggesting the market expansion is real rather than redistributive. Meanwhile, Sam Altman announced the rollout of "GPT-5.5-Cyber, a frontier cybersecurity model" to critical cyber defenders, signaling OpenAI's push into specialized enterprise applications.

The Vintage AI Experiment

In a delightfully unhinged greentext-style thread, swyx outlined the challenges of training AI models on historical data to avoid modern contamination. His hypothetical project to create a "vintage" model trained only on pre-1931 public domain texts ran into a predictable problem:
"meticulously curate hundreds of billions of pre-1931 tokens (public domain) > train it > ok! it checks out vs our FineWeb baseline! > release it > it's the most confidently racist model ever released by humankind > mfw"
The thread perfectly captures both the technical ambition and ethical complexity of building AI systems that authentically represent historical perspectives — and why some experiments are better left as thought experiments.
html_zh:
今日的AI行业充满了从基础设施到实际应用的重大发展——从OpenAI宣布新的网络安全模型，到企业开始重新构想代理时代的内部工作流程。

大模型厂商加速推进前沿功能

OpenAI的Sam Altman今日宣布了一个令人瞩目的进展：

我们将在接下来几天内开始向关键网络安全防护者推出GPT-5.5-Cyber，这是一款前沿网络安全模型。我们将与整个生态系统和政府合作，制定网络安全可信访问方案；我们希望快速帮助保护企业和基础设施。

与此同时，Google的Gemini也在用户体验方面取得突破。Josh Woodward分享了Gemini的新功能：

Gemini新功能：生成文件并导出。告诉Gemini您想创建什么以及格式，它现在会为您完成工作。现在支持：📄 Google Docs、Word (.docx) 和 PDF；📊 Google Sheets、Excel (.xlsx) 和 CSV；🖥️ Google Slides；🛠️ Markdown、LaTeX、TXT、RTF。

该功能已在全球所有平台上线，标志着AI助手从对话工具向实用生产力工具的重要转变。

代理经济的新兴模式与挑战

Stripe的数据和AI主管Emily Glassberg Sands在最新播客中深入分析了代理经济的发展现状：

互联网上出现了这种新型参与者。随着时间推移，这些代理将成为互联网上的主要参与者。这些AI公司从收入角度来看，增长速度超过了我们见过的任何以前的群体。

她指出了一个关键趋势：欺诈行为正在向上游转移。传统的支付欺诈主要是盗用信用卡，但现在攻击者开始窃取免费试用代币和计算积分。Stripe发现，在AI公司中约有7%的注册用户是多账户滥用者，而免费试用滥用在过去六个月中增长了4倍。

Aaron Levie从企业内部视角分享了他对代理工程师这一新兴岗位的思考：

开始为内部功能招聘和重新培训新的代理工程师角色，以帮助更强大的代理在关键业务流程中有效工作。我预期这种类型的角色在Box和其他公司中会变得非常重要。

开发者工具生态的演进

开发者社区对当前代理工具的实用性提出了清醒的观察。Aditya Agarwal基于大量使用OpenClaw、Hermes等工具的经验，总结了几个重要观点：

大多数对OpenClaw、HermesAgent等赞不绝口的人实际上并没有真正使用过它们。事实就是如此。代理今天是开发者产品。在用户体验的愉悦性、简单性、可靠性等方面，它们距离消费级产品还非常遥远。

他还指出了一个关键洞察：代理本质上是代码生成和工具调用的封装，而不是"生成式AI"。这种认知对于理解当前代理技术的核心机制至关重要。

Peter Steinberger展示了将代码审查功能集成到clawsweeper的进展，该系统具有自动合并功能，会循环运行直到不再发现新问题。

从历史数据中学习的挑战

swyx分享了一个发人深省的思考实验——尝试构建基于历史数据的"复古"AI模型：

互联网被AI垃圾内容污染，我们需要低背景噪音的训练数据。如果我们能时空旅行，看看100年前的祖先会对我们说什么，那会很酷。现有的复古模型都小于4B参数，我们需要一个经过对话调优的13B复古模型...最终结果：它成为了人类有史以来发布的最自信的种族主义模型。

这个幽默但深刻的观察揭示了AI训练中的一个根本性挑战：历史数据虽然"干净"，但往往承载着过时的偏见和价值观。即使技术上可行，如何处理历史遗留的社会问题仍然是AI开发者面临的重大挑战。

医疗AI的正确定位

Kevin Weil对AI在医疗领域应用提出了重要观点：

事实证明，放射科医生的工作不是读X光片，而是治愈患者。如果AI能帮助加速理解X光片的过程，放射科医生就能看到和治愈更多患者。

这个观点强调了AI作为增强工具而非替代工具的价值，特别是在需要高度专业判断的医疗领域。
